title: Quasi-coherent modules killed by the ideal of a closed subscheme are pushforwards from it
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $i_*$ and $i^*$ be the pushforward and pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], with unit $\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$. Quasi-coherent and finite type are as in [pqf-def-coherent]. (1) For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$, $i_*\mathcal G$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $\mathcal I\,(i_*\mathcal G)=0$, i.e. $as=0$ for every open $V\subseteq X$, $a\in\mathcal I(V)$ and $s\in(i_*\mathcal G)(V)$. (2) Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module with $\mathcal I\mathcal F=0$ (same meaning). Then $i^*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module and $\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; if moreover $\mathcal F$ is of finite type, so is $i^*\mathcal F$.

proof.text: A closed immersion is affine by the Mathlib instance for IsClosedImmersion. Apply affinePushforward_baseChange to the identity base-change square (i, i, id_X, id_Z), and take its quasi-coherence conjunct to prove the quasi-coherence of i_*G.

For a section a in i.ker.idealOfOpens(V), mem_idealOfOpens_iff says that a maps to zero under i.ker.subschemeι.app(V). The factorization i = i.toImage followed by i.ker.subschemeι and comp_app therefore show that i.app(V)(a) = 0. The scalar action on i_*G is restriction along this map, so a times s = 0 times s = 0 for every section s.

Both tensorPullback(i) and Mathlib pullback(i) are left adjoints to pushforward(i). Uniqueness of left adjoints gives a natural isomorphism between them. Apply the already proved isQuasicoherent_pullback instance to F and transport quasi-coherence through this isomorphism.

Put J = i.ker and let mu : J tensor F -> F be J.toModulesι whiskered by F followed by the left unitor. On a pure tensor a tensor s over V, mu has value J.toModulesι(a) times s. The ideal-range lemma puts J.toModulesι(a) in J.idealOfOpens(V), so the annihilation hypothesis makes this value zero. To prove mu = 0 globally, precompose with tensorObjIsoSheafification.inv and use injectivity of the sheafification adjunction hom equivalence. Equality of the resulting presheaf maps is checked sectionwise by tensor induction: zero and addition use linearity, while the pure-tensor case is the calculation just given.

Apply closedImmersion_unit_quotient. It supplies an epimorphic adjunction unit eta and says that image.ι(mu) is its kernel. Since factorThruImage(mu) is epi and its composite with image.ι(mu) is mu = 0, cancellation proves image.ι(mu) = 0. If g followed by eta is zero, the universal property of this kernel gives g = l followed by image.ι(mu) = 0. The preadditive cancellation criterion therefore makes eta mono. In the abelian category of modules a mono and epi is an isomorphism.

The unit-quotient lemma uses Classical.choice(nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction i), whereas this statement uses Classical.choose(exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i). Compare these two adjunctions by leftAdjointUniq. The unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app identity writes the second unit as the first unit followed by pushforward of the component of the comparison isomorphism. Both factors are isomorphisms, so the exact unit appearing in this statement is invertible.

If F is finite type, install that hypothesis as a local instance and take the first conjunct of tensorPullback_isFiniteType Z X i F. This proves finite type of tensorPullback(i)(F) directly, without requiring the support and residue-fibre assertions.

proof_origin.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS and Lemma 01B6; Morphisms, Lemma 01QY. The Lean proof uses the existing closed-immersion unit/quotient lemma (04CJ(1), proved stalkwise by 08KS), derives its zero-kernel special case by the sectionwise annihilation calculation and the sheafification adjunction, and compares the two chosen adjunctions by uniqueness.

lean.statement: theorem closedImmersion_pushforward_annihilated {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] : (∀ (G : Z.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent], ((pushforward i).obj G).IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ (V : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, V)), a ∈ i.ker.idealOfOpens V → ∀ s : Γ((pushforward i).obj G, V), a • s = 0) ∧ ∀ (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent], (∀ (V : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, V)), a ∈ i.ker.idealOfOpens V → ∀ s : Γ(F, V), a • s = 0) → ((tensorPullback i).obj F).IsQuasicoherent ∧ IsIso ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)).unit.app F) ∧ (F.IsFiniteType → ((tensorPullback i).obj F).IsFiniteType)
